newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada seeks to double Asia business.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada seeks to double Asia business.

text.p: Air Canada wants to double its Asian business within about the next three years, chief executive R. Lamar Durrett said Tuesday.

"I'd like to see our trans-Pacific operation at least double before the year 2000," he told a business group in Vancouver. Later he said he hoped the airline would double its flights, passengers and revenues in the region.
Durrett, who took up his post earlier this year, declined to say whether the company stood by the profit forecast of his predecessor, Hollis Harris.
Harris projected in February that Air Canada would earn a net profit of slightly more than C$100 million before gains in 1996.
Durrett said one difference between him and Harris was that "I'm not going to speculate on how we're doing."

He said the airline is "very concerned" about a vote in favor of a strike by Air Canada's regional airline pilots. Although the next three months will be critical, no date for strike action has been set and the airline will focus its efforts on resolving the dispute, he said.
